method: pyte 140x45 screen over a real `claude` TUI in a pty, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to a logged-in account that had never trusted the (empty, freshly made) working directory. Keys sent as raw bytes: nothing for the first screen; one Down arrow (ESC [ B) two seconds after the rows were drawn for the second. Return was then pressed and claude recorded projects[<folder>].hasTrustDialogAccepted = true and booted to its composer. An earlier run that sent Return the instant the rows appeared left the screen unchanged: the press was dropped.

screens.workspace-trust-310.captured.txt: The trust screen as 2.1.310 draws it: rows UNNUMBERED and reversed from 2.1.241 — `❯ No, exit` first and focused, `Yes, I trust this folder` under it.
screens.workspace-trust-310-yes-focused.captured: The same screen after one Down arrow: the cursor on `Yes, I trust this folder`.

sanitized: The working-directory path on the `Accessing workspace:` line was replaced with /private/tmp/dialogcap/work/trust-310 (the probe ran in a session scratch directory whose name carries local account and project names). Shorter than the original, which fit on one 140-column line either way, so no wrap changed.
